paper_metadata.title: Research on Financial Stock Market Prediction Based on the Hidden Quantum Markov Model

summary: The paper evaluates a Hidden Quantum Markov Model (HQMM) for predicting 15 Chinese stock indices and reports an average capital of 1,404,827 CNY using HQMM with GMM+MVTF discretization versus 1,390,860 CNY for classical HMM, with runtime 12 minutes versus 40 minutes. Experiments use daily SSE/SZSE data from 2018–2021 with prediction windows of 90, 180, and 360 days. The implementation appears to be a classical simulation of HQMM rather than execution on quantum hardware.

experiments.description: Hidden Quantum Markov Model (HQMM) stock trend forecasting on 15 Shanghai/Shenzhen stock indices using two discretization schemes: even discretization and GMM+MVTF discretization, compared against classical HMM baseline.

algorithm.variant: Hidden Quantum Markov Model (HQMM) with Kraus-operator training; compared under even discretization and GMM+MVTF discretization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: training iterates until DA converges; paper notes convergence after more than 40 iterations
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial density matrix ρ0 manually set; Kraus operators initialized as in prior references; GMM parameters initialized by random initialization or k-means

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous stock data are discretized into 6 observation states (S values 1–6) before HQMM training; each observation state corresponds to a Kraus operator / output matrix
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize likelihood ς = ln tr(K_Sn ··· (K_S1 ρ0 K†_S1) ··· K†_Sn) under Kraus-operator constraints ∑ K†_m K_m = I
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Kraus operators constrained by ∑ K†_m K_m = I; optimization transformed to unconstrained Stiefel-manifold update

problem_instance.description: Forecasting bullish/bearish/range-bound stock market regimes for 15 Chinese stock indices from SSE and SZSE

dataset_specification.benchmark_name: natural growth capital (NC) and classical HMM baseline
dataset_specification.preprocessing: daily open/high/low/close/volume collected; price differences computed from consecutive closing prices; data split into 30-day groups; discretized either by even binning or by GMM+MVTF

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Collect 5 daily indicators (open, high, low, close, volume); compute day-to-day closing-price differences; split into 30-day windows; either map directly to 6 discrete states or fit 1D GMM (n=5 components, K=6) and convert means/variances to trend state via MVTF
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare HQMM (even discretization and GMM+MVTF) against classical HMM across 15 stocks and 3 prediction horizons; metrics include DA, final capital (FC), comparative growth rate R, and average capital over stocks

implementation_details.classical_solver: hmmlearn, scikit-learn, GMM/EM, gradient descent on Stiefel manifold
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: pandas and NumPy preprocessing; Tushare data acquisition; backtrader used for stock data workflow
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute predicted state from minimum J_n; simulate buy/long or sell/short decisions; calculate FC, NC, and R
implementation_details.total_execution_time: 12 min for HQMM variants; 40 min for HMM baseline

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: DA rises rapidly in first <5 iterations and converges after ~40 iterations

speedup_claims.conditions: T is prediction sequence length, n is number of hidden states, w is observable space dimension
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity claim from the paper; it is not tied to a hardware benchmark.

speedup_claims.conditions: reported average total time required over the 15-stock experiment
speedup_claims.caveats: The 12 min figure applies to both HQMM variants; the paper does not separate quantum circuit runtime from classical preprocessing/training overhead.

speedup_claims.conditions: as stated in the conclusion and Table 8 comparison
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports 12 min vs 40 min, which corresponds to 70% less time, not a quantum hardware speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: linear scaling in w versus quadratic dependence on n
speedup_claims.caveats: Presented as an advantage of HQMM; no scaling experiment over varying w or n is shown.
